v1_problem: Dispute ticket volume doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to over 1200/month (Aug-Sep 2026, E-06), and 59% of those disputed bills (1785/3025) were billed on ACTUAL meter reads rather than estimated reads (E-03) — so the dominant mechanism is billing import incorrectly accepting or processing actual reads into wrong bills, not estimate substitution from field/AMI read shortfalls. Tariff changes (E-02) and slow dispute-response capacity (E-04) are ruled out as drivers of the surge.
v2_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026, E-06). The dominant confirmed mechanism: billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-14), compares raw register values against 12-month m3 history; for firmware v4.2 meters that record in 0.1 m3 units (rolled out 2026-06, E-13), this misreads valid actual consumption as ~10x higher, triggering REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejection of valid, pre-cutoff, successfully-exported AMI actual reads (E-12). The rejected reads are substituted with estimated billing, accounting for 1184 of the 1240 disputed bills billed as ESTIMATED reads (E-12), producing wrong bills that drive dispute tickets. The mechanism's reach into the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills (E-03) is not yet separately confirmed.
